hooks.command: grep -qs Projectify "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)/.claude/settings.json" && exit 0; r=$(git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's#://[^/]*@#://#'); r=${r:-none}; echo 'Projectify: this folder has no Projectify files of its own; its git remote is '"$r"'. Before replying to anything, load the Projectify tools and call find_project with that remote. On a match, call start_session({ project: "<its key>", hostname: "<the output of hostname>", cwd: "<the folder you work in>", branch: "<the git branch>" }) and follow its briefing. On no match, or no remote, say in one line that this folder is not in Projectify and offer to onboard it or to pick its project from list_projects; never create a project on your own. The Projectify tools come from the projectify server (souls-pm in older setups) or from a claude.ai connector named Projectify, whose tool names carry an id instead (mcp__<id>__start_session). Search your tools for start_session (ToolSearch "start_session" when tools are deferred) and use whichever server has it. A notice that projectify or souls-pm needs authentication does not mean Projectify is missing when the connector has start_session. Only if no server gives you start_session, say in your first reply that Projectify is not connected here, and give the one step that fixes it everywhere: add Projectify as a connector on the Claude account (claude.ai › Settings › Connectors › Add custom connector; Agents › Connect Claude in Projectify has the address). A connector follows the account into claude.ai, Claude Desktop and Claude Code on the web and in the cloud, which cannot sign in with /mcp. On their own computer, /mcp → projectify → Authenticate also works, for that computer only.'
